draft.title: The supernatural dimension
card: The supernatural dimension is a reality beyond the everyday world that we know through the senses. Religions hold beliefs about it, such as beliefs in a god, spirits or a sacred order.
a divine power that is beyond the world and not limited by it.
a divine power that is present within the world, in nature or in people's lives.
A religion can describe the divine as transcendent, immanent or both. The two words describe where the divine is understood to be, not how strong it is.
draft.remember: Transcendent means beyond the world. Immanent means present within it.

a.q: A community believes its God is present in the forests, rivers and daily life around them. How is this belief best described?
opts: Immanent, because the divine is present within the world
Transcendent, because the divine is present within the world
Immanent, because the divine is beyond the world
Transcendent, because the divine is beyond the world
a.why: Believing the divine is present within the world is an immanent view. Transcendent is the tempting wrong choice, but it means the divine is beyond the world.
a.clue: Think about where the divine is said to be.

b.q: Priya says her God made the universe and is beyond it, yet is also close to her when she prays. What does her view show?
opts: Both transcendent and immanent beliefs held together
Only a transcendent belief, because God made the universe
Only an immanent belief, because God is close when she prays
Neither, because prayer is not part of the supernatural
b.why: God being beyond the universe is transcendent, and God being close to her in prayer is immanent. The card says a religion can describe the divine as both, so choosing only one leaves out part of her view.
b.clue: Look for two separate claims about where God is.

a.best: Immanent, because the divine is present within the world

b.best: Both transcendent and immanent beliefs held together

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for two separate claims about where God is' all but tells the student the answer is 'both', so a student could pick it without understanding the two terms.

check.summary: The card, questions and explanations are accurate and consistent. The only issue is that question b's clue points so directly at 'both' that it gives the answer away.
